facts.text: The appellant took the first floor of the premises on lease on January 22, 1964 at a monthly rent of Rs. 250.

source_refs.quote: The appellant took on lease, the first floor of the premises in question from the respondent on January 22, 1964 on a monthly rent of Rs. 250.

facts.text: The respondent owned the entire premises and was occupying the ground floor.

source_refs.quote: The respondent who was the owner of the entire premises was then occupying the ground floor.

facts.text: The landlord claimed that the premises were required bona fide for residential occupation by himself and his family members.

source_refs.quote: that he required the premises bona fide for his occupation as a residence himself and his family members.

facts.text: The appellant contended that the landlord's requirement for his occupation was not bona fide.

facts.text: A prior adjudicator accepted the plea that the landlord's requirement for his occupation was not bona fide.

source_refs.quote: He also accepted his plea that the requirement of the landlord for his occupation was not bona fide.

facts.text: Both Tribunals took the view that a landlord's eviction claim made about eleven months after the letting could not be considered bona fide.

source_refs.quote: It is the view of both the Tribunals that when eviction is asked for within about I I months of the letting, the claim of the landlord cannot be considered to be bonafide.

facts.text: A prior court finding stated that the portion occupied by the landlord was not reasonably sufficient for the landlord, his wife, his son, his son's wife and their children.

source_refs.quote: the portion of the premises in the occupation of the landlord was not reaso- nably sufficient for a family consisting of the landlord, his wife, his son, son's wife and their children.

facts.text: A prior court finding stated that the premises occupied by the respondent were not reasonably suitable for his residence.
